facts.text: I have patches on my skin.
They're on my lower belly and my back.
They're a dusky red colour, and the skin there is hard and thickened.

facts.item: dark raised patch on the leg
facts.text: I have a dark, raised patch on the upper part of my right calf.

facts.item: how long the skin patches have been there
facts.text: I've had the patches on my belly and back and the patch on my calf for 2 years.
I've had IgG kappa smoldering myeloma for 13 years.
Six years ago I had similar skin patches, and at first I was told it was tumid lupus.
I used steroid creams on those earlier patches.
They only got partly better with the creams.
Back then I took lenalidomide for 9 months.
After 9 months of lenalidomide the earlier patches cleared up completely.

findings.name: skin examination
findings.result: Dusky, erythematous, indurated patches on the lower abdomen and back; firm hyperpigmented plaque on the right upper calf.

findings.name: skin biopsy of the right calf
findings.result: Dermal sclerosis with hyalinized collagen bundles extending into the subcutis; absence of CD34+ dermal dendrocytes in sclerotic zones.

findings.name: skin biopsy of the back
findings.result: Dermal sclerosis with abundant interstitial mucin confirmed by colloidal iron stain; diminished CD34+ dendrocytes in the sclerotic zone.

aliases: paraneoplastic morphea associated with IgG kappa smoldering myeloma
gold.reasoning: 1. Morphea/lupus overlap syndrome was considered — “At that time, a morphea/lupus erythematosus overlap syndrome and mixed connective tissue disease were considered in the histopathologic differential diagnosis due to the combined histopathologic features.” 2. Mixed connective tissue disease was considered — “At that time, a morphea/lupus erythematosus overlap syndrome and mixed connective tissue disease were considered in the histopathologic differential diagnosis due to the combined histopathologic features.” 3. Paraneoplastic morphea was favored — “However, a paraneoplastic process was favored, given the immunoglobulin G gammopathy and previous response to lenalidomide.”

x003.source_text: A biopsy of the back revealed dermal sclerosis with abundant interstitial mucin confirmed by colloidal iron stain and diminished CD34+ dendrocytes in the sclerotic zone.

x004.source_text: Laboratory studies confirmed persistent IgG kappa monoclonal gammopathy

x006.source_text: Whole-body CT showed no evidence of systemic mucinosis.

x005: 'All other tests were normal' does not say which tests; the record answers only a general request for other laboratory tests.

notes: Index visit: the outpatient presentation with a 2-year history of dusky indurated patches on the lower abdomen and back and a pigmented plaque on the right calf (s001, s003-s006).
The earlier episode six years before (s002) is medical history: similar lesions, the tumid lupus label he was given, and the response to steroid creams and to lenalidomide are facts.
The skin examination keeps the lesion descriptions of s001 and s003 (both describe the lesions seen at presentation).
